newsitem.title: USA: US Midcontinent unleaded basis plunges in Chicago.
newsitem.headline: US Midcontinent unleaded basis plunges in Chicago.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent spot unleaded gasoline basis continued its downward slide in Chicago Monday in the face of plentiful stocks, stepped-up production and refiner selling, traders said.
"Sun, Clark, Star. They are all selling," one trader said. "There are no buyers."

The sell-off was sparked by increased production at Clark Refining and Marketing Co's 80,515 barrel per day Blue Island, Ill., refinery, which doubled output to two million gallons a day last week following a court decision that allowed the refiner to restart a fluid catalytic cracker last week.
Weaker differentials and falling futures prices pushed basis lower across the board in the Midwest spot markets.

Chicago prompt unleaded gasoline fell to bids 3.75 cents a gallon over NYMEX December unleaded gasoline for prompt deliveries and a cent weaker for later deliveries, losing nearly two cents on the day, traders said.
Group Three unleaded made a similar downward move, ending the day at bids 3.50 cents a gallon over the print for prompt deliveries and 0.50 cent over for later deliveries.
Chicago low sulphur diesel eased to 2.50/2.75 cents a gallon over NYMEX December heating oil for prompt deliveries and was talked 0.25 cent weaker for later deliveries.

Group Three prompt low sulphur diesel differentials fell nearly two cents a gallon to 0.50/0.75 cent a gallon over the print for prompt deliveries and 0.25 cent under to even with the print for later deliveries, traders said.

Prompt high sulphur diesel was bid 1.0 cent a gallon over the print in Chicago and 0.25 cent under the print in Group Three, where later deliveries eased to 1.25 cent a gallon under the print on dormant agricultural demand.
